title: Binance fully restores withdrawals four weeks after record $6.3 billion hack attributed to North Korea
summary: Binance said on 26 November that the withdrawal suspension imposed after the 29 October hack has been fully lifted. The exchange put the theft at about $6.3 billion, the largest crypto hack on record, and the FBI attributed it to North Korean hackers it tracks as TraderTraitor. US prosecutors have filed a civil forfeiture complaint for about $1.17 billion in frozen USDC, while blockchain analysts report that stolen funds are still being laundered through bitcoin coinjoins.
impact_assessment: Observed: the largest crypto theft on record, a month-long disruption of withdrawals at the world's largest exchange, and billions of dollars frozen or seized by authorities and issuers. Potential: continued laundering of the unrecovered funds will finance North Korean state programmes in breach of sanctions, and the social-engineering and AI-tool intrusion method may be reused against other exchanges.
priority_rationale: HIGH: a record state-sponsored theft with direct sanctions-evasion and illicit-finance implications; withdrawals are restored but laundering and forfeiture actions continue.

confirmed_facts.text: Hackers stole about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance in an attack on 29 October, after which the exchange suspended withdrawals.
The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea, identifying the operation as activity it tracks as TraderTraitor.
Binance resumed withdrawals in stages from 1 November and said on 26 November that the suspension had been fully lifted.

reported_claims.text: The US Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint on 23 November seeking about $1.17 billion in USDC across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains, and said US authorities have helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the theft.
reported_claims.attributed_to: US Department of Justice (as reported by The Block)

reported_claims.text: At least $247 million of the stolen funds has passed through bitcoin coinjoins, and about $2.35 billion remained in wallets linked to the theft as of 20 November.
The attackers used fake job interviews, malicious software and compromised internal AI tools to breach Binance.
Binance says it replenished the affected assets at its own expense and that all assets remain fully backed.

international_perspectives.text: North Korea has denied involvement in the theft.

unknowns: How much of the unfrozen funds will be recovered
Full technical details of the intrusion
Whether the same method has been used against other exchanges
reassessment_triggers: Large conversion of stolen funds to cash or through sanctioned services
US court ruling on the forfeiture complaint or on the 1 December hearing on frozen assets
A similar intrusion at another exchange
monitoring_actions: Track laundering flows reported by blockchain analytics firms
Watch DOJ forfeiture and OFAC sanctions actions linked to the theft
